root_cause.text: The osnoise tracer code in `kernel/trace/trace_osnoise.c` acquired `interface_lock` before `cpus_read_lock()`, creating an लॉक-order inversion with CPU hotplug paths that take `cpus_write_lock()` and then wait on osnoise kthreads that later try to lock `interface_lock`, causing a deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description shows the deadlock sequence: task1 holds `interface_lock`, task2 enters CPU offline with `cpus_write_lock()` and calls `osnoise_cpu_die()`/`kthread_stop()`, task3 in `osnoise_sleep()` blocks on `mutex_lock(&interface_lock)`, while task1 then takes `cpus_read_lock()`, producing `[DEAD LOCK]`; the patch fixes this by swapping the order to `cpus_read_lock()` before `mutex_lock(&interface_lock)` in `osnoise_hotplug_workfn()`, `osnoise_options_write()`, and `osnoise_cpus_write()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder hotplug and interface locking in osnoise_hotplug_workfn() to use the correct synchronization order.
intent_record.what: In osnoise_hotplug_workfn(), the order of two scoped guards was changed: guard(mutex)(&interface_lock) was moved to occur after guard(cpus_read_lock)(), whereas it previously came before it.
intent_record.how: This changes the locking acquisition order at runtime so the CPU hotplug read lock is taken before interface_lock. The function's observable behavior is otherwise unchanged, but the new order likely avoids lock ordering issues or aligns with required synchronization rules when checking cpu_online(cpu).

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder locking in `osnoise_options_write()` to correctly protect option updates against CPU hotplug races.
intent_record.what: The order of two synchronization calls was changed in `osnoise_options_write()`: `mutex_lock(&interface_lock)` was moved to occur after `cpus_read_lock()`, instead of before it. No other logic in the function was modified.
intent_record.how: This changes the locking sequence so the CPU hotplug read-side lock is acquired before the interface mutex. At runtime, this helps ensure that option updates are protected against concurrent CPU hotplug activity in the intended order, reducing the chance that hotplug code observes or races with partially updated options.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder lock release in `osnoise_options_write()` to fix unsafe lock handling when updating osnoise options.
intent_record.what: The call to `cpus_read_unlock()` was moved to occur after `mutex_unlock(&interface_lock)` instead of before it in `osnoise_options_write()`.
intent_record.how: This changes the lock release order so the mutex is dropped while the CPU hotplug read-side lock is still held, which avoids a potentially unsafe lock ordering window during the option update path before optionally restarting the per-CPU kthreads.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the lock ordering in `osnoise_cpus_write()` to prevent deadlock with CPU hotplug operations.
intent_record.what: The lock acquisition order was changed in `osnoise_cpus_write()`: `cpus_read_lock()` is now taken before `mutex_lock(&interface_lock)`, and the corresponding unlock order was reversed so `mutex_unlock(&interface_lock)` happens before `cpus_read_unlock()`.
intent_record.how: This changes the runtime locking hierarchy used while copying `osnoise_cpumask`, ensuring the CPU hotplug read-side lock is held before the interface mutex. That avoids an unsafe lock ordering that could lead to deadlock or lock dependency issues when CPU hotplug paths and this write path interact.

    NMIs, IRQs, SoftIRQs, and any other system thread can cause noise to the

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the lock ordering that causes the deadlock. In `osnoise_main()` the code takes `interface_lock` after the sampling loop: `mutex_lock(&interface_lock); interval = osnoise_data.sample_period - osnoise_data.sample_runtime; mutex_unlock(&interface_lock);`. More importantly, the tracer start path creates the osnoise kthreads after initializing hooks, and the tracefs write path also takes `interface_lock` under `trace_types_lock`: `mutex_lock(&trace_types_lock); ... mutex_lock(&interface_lock); cpumask_copy(...); mutex_unlock(&interface_lock); ...`. The root cause described is that the osnoise tracer acquired `interface_lock` before `cpus_read_lock()`, creating an inversion with CPU hotplug paths that take `cpus_write_lock()` and then wait on osnoise kthreads that later try to lock `interface_lock`. In this commit version there is no visible `cpus_read_lock()` / `cpus_write_lock()` coordination around the interface lock at all, and no deadlock avoidance logic. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not present in this code.

    due to activities inside the operating system. In the context of Linux,
    NMIs, IRQs, SoftIRQs, and any other system thread can cause noise to the

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the problematic lock order in the osnoise tracer implementation. In `osnoise_main()` the code takes `interface_lock` only after `run_osnoise()` and before sleeping: `mutex_lock(&interface_lock); interval = osnoise_data.sample_period - osnoise_data.sample_runtime; mutex_unlock(&interface_lock);`. More importantly, the tracefs write path also takes `trace_types_lock` and then `interface_lock` in `osnoise_cpus_write()`: `mutex_lock(&trace_types_lock); ... mutex_lock(&interface_lock); cpumask_copy(...); mutex_unlock(&interface_lock); ... mutex_unlock(&trace_types_lock);`. The root cause described is an inversion involving `interface_lock` and `cpus_read_lock()` / CPU hotplug paths, but this commit version does not show any avoidance of that inversion because there is no `cpus_read_lock()` around the relevant per-CPU thread startup/stop or CPU mask handling. The code also starts/stops per-CPU kthreads in `start_per_cpu_kthreads()` / `stop_per_cpu_kthreads()` without any hotplug read-side protection. Since the shown code contains the lock-based interface and per-CPU thread management that can participate in the deadlock, and there is no fix present in this version, this commit is bug-introducing for the described issue.
